title: Inner Work
excerpt: Inner and outer reality as reflections of each other — and a warning about what happens to people who mistake the insight for an identity.

body: the dimensions of reality that is your thoughts and emotions are a complete reflection of the external, material reality. that is why many ancient teachings emphasize that ALL is mind. or for a better idea of what i'm talking about: ALL is the mind of God.
This relationship becomes more evident as your vibration/consciousness elevates.

This is almost impossible to pick up on or be evident at a carnal/3D/lower level of consciousness. It could be argued that this is due to the fact that during lower levels of consciousness, your mind is plagued with uncontrollable chaos. A lack of pattern/order persists through your mind. This could affirm the idea that during lower states of consciousness, life manifests to be: less divine, uncontrollable, a difficulty to make ends meet with your desires. Conversely (i know this to be true from personal experience), in higher states of consciousness, everything seems to be or manifests as completely tangible or easily under your control. in fact, reality may literally manifest in such a way that is filled with order and pattern (synchronicity). At this point, it is much easier to recognize the divinity of reality and the reflective relationship between the inner world and the outer world.

I could claim that at higher consciousnesses, the manifestation or patterns and synchronization (reflected from the order and clarity of your inner mind), allows it to be only natural to create meaning from these experiences; Ultimately, provoking 'highly conscious' individuals to easily develop new belief systems that transcend traditional/common beliefs. This also gets into why spiritual psychosis is a common symptom of these experiences (people start to feel that they or their beliefs are of high importance, and this mistakenly turns into a new identity [inflates their ego]).

However, what i am arguing in this text is that it's important to remember that divinity exists throughout all reality and experience. Meaning that even at lower consciousnesses, ones reality manifests as chaos since their own mind is filled with untamed chaos. In this level of experience, life seems very random and chaotic. Giving the illusion that reality itself is mundane, disorderly, and has no sacred nature to it (one example being atheists). This could arguably be one of the reasons why at lower consciousnesses, it is much harder to shift and alter your consciousness into a higher state. to be more clear, when your reality is chaotic, there is no synchronous patterns manifested in your world. Because of this, one tends to not find any meaning or sacred nature in their existence. This only continues to affirm the inner paradigm that we do not have any control of our reality (limiting or stopping people from 'ascending').
However, It is important to see that is only an illusion.

Most individuals (what we call monks/sages/wizards/mystics) have been able to see through this illusion through inner work and maintaining discipline in their inner paradigms (paradigms that only affirm their unity with the divine nature of reality). {i could then touch on why paradigms are important or your inner world, but this gets into the science of this whole conversation/ the law of attraction / the subconscious mind, and thats a whole lot to get into}.

What is inner work? There is no right way of doing inner work. But to put it simply, one must master/tame their mind (inner world) to then be able to begin to tame the world around you; And ultimately, recognize the beauty of the world we live in. It is no coincidence that plenty of religions refer to their 'evil'/chaos figure as one that you must fight temptation to be free. or others that say your must tame your carnal desires that confine you in lower density consciousness.
